authority.verbatim: resume, no paved roads, all terrained paths based on location wthin atlas. get creative when it comes to markings and modern guardrails from its visual direction but within our world's guidelines as some regions are more modernized than others. inklings should know how the world has existinged for the past 11 years to help with clarity

principles: Natural, unpaved terrestrial travel surfaces in every zone; existing bridges/docks/quays separate.
Modernization is local and functional, not a linear region-wide ranking; distinguish remote track, maintained local connector and serviced civic/estate corridor.

Markers and protective-edge objects may express modern functions through region-specific craft, material and maintenance. No painted traffic lanes, asphalt, concrete carriageways or generic continuous highway rail.
Metalwork or sophisticated fixtures may be proposed where regional economy supports them; no new technology system, electricity grid, reflector standard or historical installation date inferred.
A place's age does not establish the age of every fixture. Do not retrofit contemporary approvals into earlier eras.

regional_designs.name: Northern Spine
regional_designs.surface: Scree, exposed bedrock, thin compacted tracks; snow only at appropriate altitude/season.
regional_designs.low_service: Remote: irregular cairns, tool-cut stone marks, tall snow stakes; no rails on broad safe ground.
regional_designs.higher_service: Pass town or worked crossing: carefully fitted stone parapet, dark timber post-and-iron-chain edge; visible repairs and differently aged ironwork.
regional_designs.causal_basis: Local stone cutters, miners, guides; access to metalwork does not make every trail urban.
regional_designs.historical_texture: Mountain paths show generations of foot and pack use; repair date and builder unknown.

established_service.surface: Worn scree and exposed stone with compacted earth at sheltered passes; snow only at supported altitude/season.
established_service.wayfinding: Notched timber direction posts and locally worked iron markers at existing pass junctions.
established_service.edge: Short stone or timber-and-iron boundaries only at established exposed edges.
established_service.ordinary_use: Guides, pack traffic and seasonal supply.
established_service.aging: Older rock and repaired posts; no dates asserted.

visual_study.composition: Single live-action establishing photograph, rain-dark compacted earth and loose natural gravel, mature wet foliage, diffuse early light, freestanding old stone waymarker with locally forged iron fitting, no readable invented directions. If no real edge hazard is visible, no rail; an alternate material-only study may explore weathered timber posts with custom iron rail at an abstract exposed edge, without establishing a new structure. No asphalt, concrete, painted lanes, standardized traffic signs, highway guardrail, vehicle identity, coastline or island.
